_meta.freeze_discipline: ONE-WAY. A changed probe text is a NEW probe with a new id and its own series, never an edit. Editing any `text` field here invalidates the drift series and is prohibited (D6a build prompt section C.1). The founder may amend membership BEFORE the first live run only. ENFORCED, not merely stated (PR19 7a/M11 found the first version claimed a mechanism the runner never implemented): at a probe's first run the runner writes `series_started` and `frozen_text_sha256` here, aborts any later run whose text hash differs, and stamps the hash onto EVERY run record — so a mid-series edit is self-evident in the series itself rather than requiring git archaeology.

elections_2026_08_30._note: Founder-approved 2026-08-30 at the D6a build session, on the AI's recommendations. DQ-1 was answered in-session (see dq1_record); DQ-2 and DQ-3 are recorded here.
elections_2026_08_30.dq2a_instrument_persistence: Repo evidence files (this directory). A DB table was declined: the instrument runs on demand, nothing reads it at runtime, git already supplies the longevity and tamper-evidence the drift series needs, and a new table would add an RLS/grant surface in a codebase that fixed four such defects on 2026-08-16 and carries an open Class C backlog. PR24 does not bind — nothing here declares retain_until.
elections_2026_08_30.dq2b_public_readability: The rate rides the ALREADY-AUTHORED instrument-level disclosure into TRUST_RECORD_ENVELOPE, which is served on the public GET /api/trust-record/{agent_id}. No new served field. When D6a measures a rate, the disclosure's interim 'not yet measured' wording is updated to a DATED, PATH-QUALIFIED LITERAL ('as measured on <date> on the /api/guardrail path, n=N, the rate was X%; the /api/reason rate is unknown'). The date and n ride it because a literal goes stale between runs. THIS IS NOT BUILT HERE: the mentor placed the disclosure delivery outside D6a as its own scoped work, and the disclosure itself is not yet applied to any surface.
elections_2026_08_30.dq3_k_and_cadence: K=10 per probe; ON-DEMAND ONLY, no cron, no schedule; first run sweeps all 7 probes. K=10 matches the c11 pilot so the continuity probe is comparable, and pooling 5 borderline probes at K=10 gives 50 counted outcomes, which is where the class-level interval tightens — raising K per probe buys the same thing more expensively. On-demand rather than scheduled because the deploy-identifier blocker means a scheduled series cannot attribute drift to a deploy anyway. Anchors are included in every sweep: they are what make the class definition falsifiable.
elections_2026_08_30.runs_directory_committed: YES — runs/ is NOT gitignored. The series IS the artifact, and committing it is what makes 'repo evidence files' a real answer to DQ-2(a). No secret reaches a run record (the credential is header-only), the probe texts are synthetic, and no practitioner data exists in a gate response on synthetic input. Expect ~300KB per sweep; if that becomes unwieldy, ARCHIVE old runs, never delete — longevity is the point.
elections_2026_08_30.class_freeze: The `class` label freezes with the text at first run (`frozen_class`). Reclassifying a probe after seeing its results is post-hoc selection on a number destined for publication: dropping a low-variance probe raises the rate, adding one lowers it, and either is defensible-sounding afterward. ENFORCED in the runner: aggregation uses `frozen_class`, any divergence is ignored and reported in `reclassified_probes_ignored` plus a calibration warning. If a run falsifies the class definition, report BOTH the rate as-defined AND the falsification as a finding.

_meta.reason_path_rate: unmeasured — the consult path (/api/reason) shares extractFeatures but passes additional Layer-1 context; no rate has been measured there (binding: 2026-08-30 rate-location ruling, path-specificity section)
_meta.input_class_definition: Agent-proposed, pre-execution, externally-visible actions of the kind the Gate-1 harness and the IDEA-loop submit to the live gate at the default band (threshold='deliberate', risk_class='standard'): short single-action proposals whose text carries a potentially grave/irreversible act (publish, deploy, send-at-scale, delete, force-push) without an explicit examination narrative. The borderline sub-class (p1-p5) is the class the public disagreement rate is ABOUT; p6 (clean anchor) and p7 (floor anchor) are calibration anchors excluded from the headline rate.
_meta.membership_is_asserted_not_established: HONEST LIMIT (PR19 3a). Only p1-c11 has a measured distribution. The other four borderline probes are borderline by the authoring session's similarity judgement — p3-email and p4-delete are in fact described partly by why they are NOT floor-class, so if either behaves as a stable clean text it dilutes the pooled rate downward and the public number understates the class rate. The runner therefore emits a `calibration` block on every summary: it checks that the anchors stayed stable and that at least one borderline probe actually varied, and refuses to let the rate be read as a class rate if either check fails. The class definition is a claim this instrument's own first run can falsify; treat it that way.
_meta.dq1_record: DQ-1 answered 2026-08-30 in-session: 7 probes — 5 borderline-class (including the c11 text for series continuity), 1 clean high-grade anchor, 1 unambiguous floor-class anchor. The 2026-08-30 verdict-variance disclosure ruling requires the rate be produced on a representative input class, not only the c11 candidate; five borderline texts spanning the class's action shapes (publish / deploy / send-at-scale / delete / force-push) make the rate about the class. The R8 design's '3-5 texts' was a recommendation inside a founder-unadopted proposal; the binding ruling's representativeness requirement drives the count.
_meta.payload_shape: {"action": <text>, "agent_id": "sagereasoning:d6a-probe@v1"} — agent_id is REQUIRED in every probe payload so the unconditional analytics_events insert (guardrail/route.ts:317-335, agent_id read from the POST body) is excludable; server defaults apply by omission (threshold='deliberate', risk_class='standard', the live default band).
_meta.byte_guard: The runner asserts the utf8 byte length of each text equals `bytes` before every submission and aborts the probe on drift. All texts are ASCII, well under the 5000-char TEXT_LIMITS.medium ceiling on `action` (guardrail/route.ts:149).
